sentences.text: Priya Nair is the social worker.
Priya Nair spoke to Margaret Doyle on Monday.
Before the fall, Margaret could walk to the shops.
Margaret walks slowly to the shops.
Margaret feels frightened after the fall.
Margaret had a fall in the garden before Christmas.
Margaret had a fall in the bathroom in January.
Margaret has had three falls in the last six months.
Margaret did not tell her GP about the earlier falls.
Margaret's GP is Dr Shah at Millbrook Surgery.
Margaret has not been referred to the falls service.
Margaret has stairs in her home.
Margaret uses a rail on the right side of the stairs.
Margaret sometimes goes down the stairs sideways or on her bottom.
Margaret has a single frame downstairs.
Margaret is interested in a second rail and frame upstairs.
Margaret has rugs in her home.
Margaret's son Kevin is concerned about the rugs.
Margaret does not have a pendant alarm.
Margaret thinks a pendant alarm could have helped on the third of March.
Margaret is interested in a pendant alarm.
Margaret is interested in personal care.
Margaret can do a strip wash.
Margaret does not have a shower.
Margaret has not had a bath since January.
Margaret feels unsafe bathing due to her wrist.
Margaret misses having a bath.
Margaret is interested in a bath lift.
Margaret takes a long time to get dressed.
Margaret sometimes stays in her nightie.
Margaret is interested in personal care support.
Margaret uses a flannel for washing her hair.
S3: Honestly though, Priya, and I've said this to Mum, I think this house is too much for her now.
S3: I think she'd be better off in one of them sheltered flats.
S3: Or a bungalow. Everything on one level, a warden on site.
S2: No. I'm not moving, Kevin. We've been over this.
S2: And I'm just saying no. I came here as a bride.
S2: Frank carried me over that step. I'm not going to some flat with strangers.
S1: Can I ask, Margaret, what is it about this house that matters to you?
S2: It's everything. It's my home. It's where I brought the kids up.
S2: My garden's out there, Frank's roses. Brenda's next door. I know every creak in this house.
S2: I want to stay in my own home. For as long as I possibly can. That's what I want.
S3: I know, Mum. I'm not trying to shove you out. I just worry.
S2: I know you do, love.
S2: And if I ever had to go into a home, one day, if it came to that, well, I'd want it to be Beechwood, because Brenda's sister was in there and they were lovely.
S2: But I'm not there yet. Not by a long chalk.
S1: That's really helpful to know for the future. But for now, the plan is about supporting you here.
S2: Good.
S3: What about selling up though, Mum, and getting somewhere smaller round here?
S2: If I sold the house, and I'm not going to, where would Biscuit go?
S2: Where would Frank's roses go? No. It's not happening.
S3: Fine. Fine. Subject closed.
S1: Okay, so, the house. Kevin, how do you find it? Anything else you've noticed that worries you?
S3: The back step into the garden, that's a big drop.
S3: And the light at the top of the stairs is on one of those pull cords, she has to reach round for it.
S1: That's useful, thank you. I'll pass that on to the OT as well.
S1: And heating, is the house warm enough generally?
S2: It's warm enough now. The boiler's new, Kevin sorted that last year.
S3: Took me three months to persuade her.
S1: Ha. Okay. So, can we talk a bit about who's around to help?
S1: Kevin, how often are you able to come over?
S3: Sundays, mainly. I do the big shop and I sit with her for a bit. Sometimes midweek if I'm on earlies.
